01-course-introduction.q: Which notation does this course use for ER diagrams, including on exams?
In relational terminology, a row of a table is also called a…
JSON and XML are examples of which kind of data?
01-course-introduction.explain: Structured = tables/rows. Semi-structured = some structure but flexible (XML, JSON). Unstructured = images, audio, video.

01-course-introduction.q: Where is the description of a database's data stored?
Two withdrawals hit the same bank account at the same instant and both must debit correctly. Which database challenge is this?
What is the order of the course project pipeline?
options: SQL → E-R Model → Load Data → Relational Tables → Web Interface
E-R Model → Relational Tables (Normalization) → Load Data → SQL → Web Interface
Web Interface → SQL → E-R Model → Load Data
Load Data → E-R Model → SQL → Normalization

01-course-introduction.q: How many relations must the course project have at minimum?
01-course-introduction.explain: At least 5 (7+ recommended), with 2 holding a few thousand tuples and 1 holding hundreds.

01-course-introduction.q: What is the weight of the final exam in SE 3309?

options: The DBMS software together with the data (sometimes the applications too)

02-introduction-to-databases.q: What is the defining weakness of a file-based system?
options: Each program defines and manages its own data — there's no central data definition
It is always slower than a database

02-introduction-to-databases.q: In the DreamHome case study, Sales and Contracts each keep their own PropertyForRent and Client files. What problem does this show?
The system catalog makes a database system…
02-introduction-to-databases.explain: Because the structure lives in the catalog, the same DBMS can work with many different databases.

02-introduction-to-databases.q: Adding a new field to a record doesn't require rewriting the DBMS access programs. This is…
Hiding physical storage details and presenting a conceptual view via a data model is called…
Which DBMS language specifies data types, structures and constraints?
02-introduction-to-databases.explain: DDL = Data Definition Language. DML = Data Manipulation Language (select, insert, delete, update).

02-introduction-to-databases.q: Which is NOT a benefit of views?
options: Eliminates the need for a DBMS
Presents a consistent picture even if the underlying database changes

02-introduction-to-databases.q: In the five components of the DBMS environment, which acts as the bridge between the machine side and the human side?
02-introduction-to-databases.explain: Machine side: hardware, software. Bridge: data. Human side: procedures, people.

02-introduction-to-databases.q: Who manages the physical DBMS and database?
02-introduction-to-databases.explain: The DA manages the organization's data resource; the DBA manages the physical DBMS and database.

02-introduction-to-databases.q: An end user who writes their own queries is a ____ end user.
Which generation of database systems introduced relational databases?
02-introduction-to-databases.explain: First = hierarchical and network. Second = relational. Third (debated) = object-relational, OO, NoSQL/NewSQL.

02-introduction-to-databases.q: Which is a disadvantage of DBMSs?
In a three-tier architecture, where does business/data-processing logic live?
A four-tier architecture adds which component compared to three-tier?
options: A web server between the client and application server

02-introduction-to-databases.q: What does a distributed DBMS do?
options: Manages a distributed database and makes the distribution transparent to users

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: Staff, Branch and Client are examples of…
03-entity-relationship-modeling.explain: An entity type is a group of objects with the same properties. One specific staff member is an entity occurrence.

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: What is the degree of a relationship?
options: The number of attributes it has
The number of participating entity types

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: Staff registers a client at a branch. What degree is the Registers relationship?
Staff (supervisor) supervises Staff (supervisee). This is a…
03-entity-relationship-modeling.explain: Same entity type participating more than once in different roles; role names clarify the purpose.

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: address = street + city + postcode is what kind of attribute?
telNo [1..3] on Branch is what kind of attribute?
/totalStaff, shown with a leading slash, is…

options: A minimal set of attributes that uniquely identifies each occurrence of an entity type

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: A candidate key made of two or more attributes is a…
Why is Preference a weak entity type?
options: It is existence-dependent on Client — it can't exist without its owner
It participates in a ternary relationship

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: Multiplicity is made up of which two restrictions?
"All branches are managed, but not all staff manage a branch" describes…
03-entity-relationship-modeling.explain: Participation = whether all (mandatory) or some (optional) occurrences participate. Cardinality = the maximum number.

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: Each newspaper advertises many properties and each property may be in many newspapers. This is…

options: Zero, or three, or six through eight

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: Staff –Has– Division –Operates– Branch, both 1:*. You can't tell which branch SG37 works at. This is a…
03-entity-relationship-modeling.explain: Fan trap: the pathway is ambiguous. Fix by restructuring to Division → Branch → Staff.

03-entity-relationship-modeling.q: Branch –Has– Staff –Oversees (optional)– Property. Property PA14 has no overseeing staff, so you can't find its branch. This is a…
03-entity-relationship-modeling.explain: Chasm trap: the pathway doesn't exist for some occurrences. Fix by adding Branch –Offers– Property directly.

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: Why was the EER model introduced?
options: Basic ER concepts aren't expressive enough for newer, more demanding applications

04-enhanced-er-modeling.explain: A subclass occurrence and its superclass occurrence are the same real-world object.

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: What are the problems with using only a single AllStaff entity for every kind of staff?
options: Shared attributes are described more than once
Lots of nulls and no way to model subclass-only relationships
It can't have a primary key

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: What are the problems with using only separate subclasses and no superclass?
options: Shared concepts get described more than once and must be kept consistent

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: Starting with Staff and splitting out Manager, SalesPersonnel and Secretary by their distinguishing characteristics is…
04-enhanced-er-modeling.explain: Specialization is top-down (maximize differences). Generalization is bottom-up (minimize differences).

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: Noticing Staff, PrivateOwner and Client all have a number and a name, and pulling those into Person, is…
In UML, specialization/generalization is drawn with…
options: A hollow triangle on the superclass end

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: Every Owner must be a PrivateOwner or a BusinessOwner, but never both. Which constraint?
Staff may be a Supervisor or a Manager or neither, but not both. Which constraint?

options: Nondisjoint — a member can belong to several subclasses
Every member is in exactly one subclass
No member is in a subclass

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: Why does Supervisor exist as a subclass even though it has no attributes of its own?
options: So that it (not every staff member) takes part in the Supervises relationship

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: Aggregation is drawn with ____ and composition with ____.
options: a filled diamond; a hollow diamond
a hollow diamond; a filled diamond
a dashed line; a solid line

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: Which is true of composition but NOT aggregation?
options: There is a whole and a part
The part cannot exist without the whole and belongs to exactly one whole

04-enhanced-er-modeling.q: Newspaper displays Adverts, and an advert can't exist without its newspaper. This is…

04-enhanced-entity-relationship-modeling.q: A Manager has staffNo, name, position, salary from Staff plus mgrStartDate and bonus. This is…
Which relationship could a single Staff entity NOT express well, motivating a Manager subclass?
options: Manager Manages Branch — a relationship only managers take part in

04-enhanced-entity-relationship-modeling.q: {Mandatory, And} means every superclass member is in…
{Optional, And} means every superclass member is in…
Person → Staff → Supervisor/Manager is an example of…
options: A specialization hierarchy (a subclass with its own subclasses)

04-enhanced-entity-relationship-modeling.q: A shared subclass is one that…
options: Has more than one superclass and inherits from all of them

04-enhanced-entity-relationship-modeling.q: In the DreamHome EER branch view, the separate POwns and BOwns relationships became…
options: A single Owns relationship to a new Owner superclass

04-enhanced-entity-relationship-modeling.q: Branch Has Staff and Branch Offers PropertyForRent are drawn as aggregations. Which is the whole?
With aggregation, can the part be shared by many wholes?
options: Only if it's a weak entity

04-enhanced-entity-relationship-modeling.q: Where does the (E)ER diagram sit in database design?
options: It is the conceptual data model, before the logical (relational) model

05-logical-database-design.q: Logical database design is tied to a ____ but independent of a ____.
options: specific data model (e.g. relational); particular DBMS and physical details

05-logical-database-design.q: In the relational model, "degree" is ____ and "cardinality" is ____.
options: number of rows; number of columns
number of attributes; number of tuples
number of keys; number of relations
number of tables; number of databases

05-logical-database-design.q: Which is NOT a property of relations?
options: Each cell holds exactly one atomic value
The order of attributes is significant
All values of an attribute come from the same domain
Any candidate key not selected as the primary key
A key that can be null
No attribute of the primary key can be null
Foreign keys must match or be wholly null
There can be only one candidate key

05-logical-database-design.q: Referential integrity says a foreign key value must…
options: Match a candidate key value in its home relation, or be wholly null
Be the primary key of its own relation

05-logical-database-design.q: Is null the same as zero or an empty string?
options: No — null is the absence of a value (unknown or not applicable)
Post the "many" side's PK into the "one" side
Post the "one" side's PK into the "many" side as a FK

05-logical-database-design.q: Client States Preference is 1..1 on both sides. How is it mapped?
For a 1:1 relationship mandatory on one side only, which entity is the parent?
05-logical-database-design.explain: The optional-participation entity is the parent; its PK is copied into the child.

options: Post one PK into the other relation
Create a new relation with both PKs as FKs (together forming the PK), plus the relationship's attributes

05-logical-database-design.q: Why can't a *:* relationship be mapped with a foreign key in one of the entity relations?
options: It would need many values in one cell, breaking atomicity

05-logical-database-design.q: Viewing (clientNo, propertyNo, dateView, comment) has PK clientNo, propertyNo. When would dateView need to join the key?
options: If a client could view the same property more than once

05-logical-database-design.q: For a {Mandatory, Or} superclass/subclass, the guideline is…
options: One for the superclass and one per subclass

05-logical-database-design.q: For a {Mandatory, And} superclass/subclass, the guideline is…
How is a multi-valued attribute like Branch telNo [1..3] mapped?
options: Keep all numbers in one cell
A new relation for the attribute with the owner's PK as a FK

05-logical-database-design.q: In the Registers ternary mapping, only Client is on a "many" end. What's the PK of Registration?
In the staff view, the optional Supervisor subclass and the Supervises relationship become…
options: A recursive supervisorStaffNo FK in Staff

final.q: A database is formally a ____ collection of logically related data plus a description of that data.
A company's billing and shipping apps each define their own customer files, which drift out of sync. Which approach caused this?
A DBMS's controlled access may include which of these?
options: Security, integrity, concurrency control, recovery control and a user-accessible catalog

final.q: A registrar should see student grades but HR should see only names and departments. Which DBMS feature fits?
Instructions for starting/stopping the DBMS and doing backups belong to which DBMS-environment component?
Hosting your database on Amazon RDS with a shared database but separate schemas per tenant is an example of…
A solicitor arranges a bid for a buyer, supported by a financial institution. Degree of Arranges?
In the ternary Registers relationship, fixing a Staff/Branch pair still allows several Clients. This describes multiplicity of…
options: One entity type when the other n−1 values are fixed

final.q: Each staff member oversees zero or more properties; each property is overseen by zero or one staff. This is…
Which multiplicity means "one or many"?
A model suggests a relationship between two entities, but for some occurrences the pathway doesn't exist. This is a…
How do you fix a fan trap?
options: Restructure the relationships so the pathway between occurrences is unambiguous

final.q: Which pair correctly describes the two directions to a superclass/subclass hierarchy?
options: Specialization: top-down, maximize differences; generalization: bottom-up, minimize differences

final.q: Every member of a subclass is also a member of the superclass. Must every superclass member be in a subclass?
options: Only if the participation constraint is mandatory
Only if the disjoint constraint is And

final.q: A university Person can be both a Student and an Employee, and every Person is at least one. Which constraint?
A Car has Wheels; a wheel can be moved to another car and exists on its own. Which relationship best fits?
In the relational model, a domain is…
options: The set of allowable values for one or more attributes

final.q: In the Branch instance with 4 columns and 5 rows, what are the degree and cardinality?
"Cardinality" in ER modeling vs the relational model:
options: ER: max relationship occurrences per entity; relational: number of tuples in a relation
ER: number of rows; relational: number of columns

final.q: A foreign key can reference…
options: A candidate key of some relation, including the same relation
final.explain: e.g. supervisorStaffNo in Staff references Staff(staffNo).

final.q: A composite foreign key has one part filled and one part null. Is this allowed under referential integrity?
options: No — it must match fully or be wholly null
Only if the PK is null

final.q: In the PK/FK mechanism, the relation whose key gets copied is the ____, and the one receiving it is the ____.
What is the correct order of the first steps for deriving relations?
options: Strong entities → weak entities → 1:* → 1:1 → 1:1 recursive → superclass/subclass → *:* → complex → multi-valued attributes

final.q: When mapping a strong entity with composite attribute name (fName, lName), the relation includes…
options: Only the simple parts fName and lName

final.q: Why can't a weak entity's primary key be finalized when it is first mapped?
options: Its key is derived partly or fully from its owner, which needs the relationship mapped first

final.q: Every client must be registered by a staff member (1..1 on the Staff side). What does this mean for staffNo in Client?
Most cars are used by staff, but only a few staff use cars (optional on both sides). Which mapping avoids lots of nulls?
options: Make Staff the parent and post staffNo into Car

final.q: For a 1:1 recursive relationship optional on both sides, the mapping is…
options: A single relation with two copies of the PK
A new relation to represent the relationship

final.q: For an {Optional, Or} superclass/subclass, the guideline is…
options: One for the superclass plus one per subclass

final.q: For an {Optional, And} superclass/subclass, the guideline is…
options: Two relations: one for the superclass, one for all subclasses combined with discriminators

final.q: In a complex (n-ary) relationship mapping, which foreign keys generally form part of the primary key?
Each phone number belongs to exactly one branch. In Telephone (telNo, branchNo), what is the PK?
final.explain: Because telNo is an alternate key of Branch, it can be the PK alone. If numbers could be shared, the key would be telNo, branchNo.

final.q: In the final staff-view relations, why is ownerNo in PropertyForRent awkward in SQL?
options: It references two relations (PrivateOwner and BusinessOwner), but an SQL FK can only reference one table

final.q: In Lease, deposit and duration are…
options: Derived attributes computed from rent and lease dates
